subject: SKU mapping + quantization guidance for CloudLine pilot
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@cloudline.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudline.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask + SKU mapping details (CloudLine)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudLine is excited to move to a short pilot to validate latency and unit cost for our search summarization path. Procurement asked me to send a short RFP + specific SKU mapping so we can compare offers from a couple vendors.

Attached: CloudLine_RFP_SA.pdf (requirements + success criteria). Highlights:
- 2 month pilot, ~5M tokens/mo steady state, peak bursts to 30 reqs/sec for short windows.
- Mixed workload: 40% short completions (~200 tokens), 60% long chat-like flows (~1500 tokens).
- Security: SOC2 required, VPC option preferred but not a blocker for pilot.

Questions for Redwood:
1) How do you recommend we map pilot workloads to your SKU/commit tiers?
2) Any guidance on quantization levels that preserve answer quality for the long chat flows?
3) Will caching/prefix reuse materially change unit economics for our expected mix?

Can you send a short SKU-level proposal and any technical notes your team needs to size the pilot? Procurement will want a line-item pricing workbook.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudLine

-- attachment: CloudLine_RFP_SA.pdf (pdf, 210KB)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Samir Gupta <samir@cloudline.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask + SKU mapping details (CloudLine)

Samir — thanks for the RFP and the clear success criteria. We're happy to propose a pilot structure and the SKU mapping that will reflect both burst/steady state economics and the impact of caching + quantization.

Quick answers up front:
- We'll propose a 2-tier SKU map: steady-state commit (tokens/mo) + burst reserve for short windows. That lets you get predictable unit price while keeping headroom.
- For the long chat flows, we recommend int8 quantization for the majority of traffic; we can offer int4 trials on a subset to validate quality vs. cost.
- Prefix/KV caching should reduce token compute for repeated user funnels — estimate ~18-28% token-cost reduction in your mix once warm.

I'll attach a draft pricing workbook and a short technical note (quant_recs_snippet.md) with recommended quant targets per model family. Can Jordan and Neha weigh in on concession sizing for a two-month pilot (we expect procurement will request credit splits / rebate language)?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

-- attachments: pricing_schedule_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB); quant_recs_snippet.md (text, 6KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com; neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask + SKU mapping details (CloudLine)

Olga / Neha — looped in to propose a concrete commercial shape for procurement. Running assumptions: 2 months, 5M tokens/mo baseline (10M total), 30 reqs/sec burst windows (short duration), pilot start Sept 1.

Proposed commercial construct (pilot):
- Commit SKU: 250K token-band tiers priced inline with our starter commit (list in attached workbook).
- Burst buffer: reserve 10% of expected peak as on-demand at a slightly higher per-token.
- Credit split: offer $12K in total credits applied as follows: 70% usage credit (applied to token charges), 30% professional services credit (ops support & pilot tuning).
- SLA/credits: standard pilot SLA, with a one-time clause in SOW that allows a single 5% invoice credit if latency targets not met in >4/8 windows.

Technical concessions / quant guidance:
- For long chat flows: recommend int8 quantized weights with KV cache enabled. Enable per-conversation prefix caching for re-used context (expect 18-28% compute reduction after warm).
- Suggest a split test: route 10% of traffic to int4 quantized instances (lower cost) for 2 weeks and run automated evals (we'll provide eval harness). If quality drift <= 2.5% A/B loss, we expand int4 to a further 20% with additional QA.
- Ops note: We will surface token/latency breakouts in Console and provide a short runbook to help CloudLine tune batch sizes safely.

Neha — can you confirm whether the $12K credit is something we can sign off on for a pilot before legal approval? If not, propose an alternate $8K credit with 80/20 split.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Samir — following up with the pilot SKU mapping and a compact commercial pitch based on your RFP. Summary below and attached workbook for procurement line-items.

Executive summary:
- Pilot length: 2 months (Sept 1 — Oct 31)
- Expected tokens: 10M total (5M/mo steady) with short bursts up to 30 reqs/sec
- Commercial: $0.0009 / token on committed bands, burst at $0.00125 / token.
- Credits: $12,000 total (70% usage credit / 30% services) applied as a one-time offset on pilot invoices.
- Technical: default to int8 quantization + KV/prefix caching. We will run a 10% int4 split test for two weeks; results reported in Console and a short eval doc.

What we need from you to finalize DOCS:
1) Procurement confirmation that pilot dates and the $12K credit are acceptable.
2) Point of contact for SOC2 artifact transfer (we'll send a secure link to the SOC2 bundle).
3) Any required PO number or internal purchase flow to issue the pilot SOW.

Attachments: pricing_schedule_v3.xlsx (line-item pricing workbook), quant_recs_snippet.md (brief quant recommendations).

Best,
